好，sensor_msgs已经是依赖了。现在我需要设计三个任务。

先想清楚 T1、T2、T3各自的设计。

### T3：协议加 seq/flagscore层 `chassis_packet.hpp`：
- `ChassisCommand`加 `uint8_t seq =0;`
- `ChassisOdometryPacket`加 `bool fault`、`bool uart_timeout`、`bool estop_input`、`bool overcurrent`（或者用一个 flags位域 + `std::optional<uint8_t> last_cmd_seq`）
- `EncodeMickSpeedCommand`输出7字节 payload- `DecodeMickBinaryPacket`读 payload≥12，flags在 offset12，last_cmd_seq在 offset13- `ChassisStatePacket`加 fault flags？

关键设计考量：向后兼容。payload只有6字节的下行帧（旧主机）和7字节（新主机），MCU侧兼容是固件的事。主机侧发送现在改成7字节——这会不会破坏现有 e2e？e2e用的是 mock_physical_chassis.py，它解析文本协议。让我确认 mock是否也要同步。

mock_physical_chassis.py用文本协议（ODOM/STATE）。而 `protocol: text`是默认，e2e都用 text。所以改二进制编码不影响 e2e。但 `test_chassis_packet.cpp`的 `MickFrameRoundTripSpeedCommand`只断言 ≥7字节，不会挂。

不过要注意：是否有测试断言 `EncodeMickSpeedCommand`的精确长度或 sum8？我看一下 test_chassis_packet.cpp全文和 test_serial_udp_backend.cpp。

另外 seq的维护在哪？`ChassisCommand`是值类型，seq应该由 backend维护（每帧 +1），而不是调用方。所以 `SerialBackend` / `UdpBackend`里维护一个 `uint8_t seq_`。这样 `ChassisCommand.seq`由 backend填充。但 `EncodeMickSpeedCommand(command)`是纯函数，如果从 command读 seq就要求调用方设置。

更干净：`SerialBackend`/`UdpBackend`各持有一个 `uint8_t tx_seq_`，每次 `WriteCommand`前 `cmd.seq = tx_seq_++`。`EncodeMickSpeedCommand`把它编码进去。

帧长14字节。

T3还需要「命令送达率」指标。这个要落在哪里？`link_quality.cpp`有 frames_lost/frames_crc_error。我可以加一个 `RecordCommandAck(uint8_t seq)`之类，但需要考虑窗口。简单做法：

在 `LinkQualitySnapshot`加 `uint64_t commands_acked` / `commands_sent` / `delivery_rate`。在 `LinkQualityMonitor`加 `RecordCommandSent()`和 `RecordCommandAcked()`。送达率的计算：需要滑动窗口或累计。用累计更简单，但会被长期稀释。用一个小窗口（最近64个 seq的 bitmap）最好——uint64 bitmap，正好64位。

设计：`LinkQualityMonitor`维护：
- `uint64_t sent_bitmap_`：记录已发 seq的位（bit = seq %64）
- `uint64_t ack_bitmap_`：记录已确认 seq的位- seq前进时，如果跨过一代，要清零。

嗯，这个复杂度不低。用更简单但够用的方案：**累计计数器 +滑动窗口对齐现有风格**。

其实最简单且语义正确：**用「最近 N个已发送命令中有多少被回显确认」**。实现：
- `std::array<bool,64> sent_window_` + `std::array<bool,64> ack_window_`按 seq%64索引-每发一帧：`sent_window_[seq%64]=true; ack_window_[seq%64]=false; ++sent_total_`
-每收一帧带 last_cmd_seq：`ack_window_[seq%64]=true; ++acked_total_`
-从 bitmap算：在窗口内（最近64个 seq的范围内）sent且 acked的比例但如果只看 bitmap的64位，老数据会残留。需要知道哪些位是"当前代"的。用 seq的绝对值：记录 `latest_sent_seq_`，则有效范围是 [latest_sent_seq_-63, latest_sent_seq_]。对范围内每个 seq检查 bit。

这个可以实现，但有点绕。考虑到这是台架演示项目，我用更务实的方法：

**累计计数 +一代内的滑动**：维护 `sent_total_`和 `acked_total_`，送达率 = acked/sent（累计）。同时给一个 `delivery_window_`用固定64位 bitmap只统计最近一代。

我先实现累计版 + bitmap窗口版，因为 bitmap版本才是真的有价值（累计会被稀释）。

让我用这种方式：

```cppclass LinkQualityMonitor {
 //命令送达率（v2 T3）：最近 window个下行命令里有多少被 MCU回显确认。
 //用64位代数位图：bit i表示"seq %64 == i的那个 seq已发送/已确认"。
 //代数通过 sent_epoch_high_判定，避免64帧以前的残留位污染统计。
 void RecordCommandSent(uint8_t seq);
 void RecordCommandAck(uint8_t seq);
```

实现细节：uint8_t seq回绕0..255，而 bitmap是64位，所以 seq%64有4个 seq共享一个位。这意味着如果 seq前进 >64，旧位会被新 seq覆盖——这正好是我们想要的（覆盖即重置）。但要保证 sent和 ack的覆盖同步。

最简单可靠：用 `std::array<uint8_t,64>`存 `(seq_key)或者0xFF表示无效`。嗯，还是复杂。

**换个更务实的方案**：直接统计「最近64个 seq范围内」：
-维护一个 `std::deque<uint8_t> recent_sent_`最多64个-维护 `std::unordered_set<uint8_t>`的 ack集合...但 seq回绕会重复。

算了。**最务实**：用累计计数，但只统计"能从 ack映射回 sent"的。既然 seq是8位，最近256帧内不会有歧义。

实际上，让我用 **`std::array<int32_t,64> slot_seq_`**记录每个 slot当前存的是哪个"绝对 seq"。绝对 seq用 uint64递增：

```
uint64_t absolute_seq = seq_counter_ //单调递增，发一帧 +1slot = absolute_seq %64```
但 MCU回显的是 uint8 seq，主机需要把 uint8映射回绝对 seq。可以：`if (uint8 seq == (sent_abs_ &0xFF))`直接匹配最新，或者用"回绕计数"估算：`abs = sent_abs_ - ((sent_abs_ - uint8seq) &0xFF)`。

这是标准做法：
```cppuint64_t Delta(uint8_t ack_seq) const {
 return (sent_abs_ - ack_seq) &0xFF; //0..255}
```
如果 delta <=63，就在窗口内。然后 abs = sent_abs_ - delta。

嗯，我觉得这个有点过度设计了。**台架演示项目，指标要真实但不能复杂到没法测。**

我采用一个中间方案：

`ChassisLinkHealth`加字段：
- `uint64 frames_command_sent` —下行命令帧总数- `uint64 frames_command_acked` — MCU回显确认的帧数- `float64 command_delivery_rate` — acked/sent（最近64帧滑动）

滑动用 **`std::array<uint8_t,64>`存每个槽的绝对 seq低8位 +是否 ack**：

```cppstruct CommandSlot { uint8_t seq =0; bool valid=false; bool acked=false; };
std::array<CommandSlot,64> cmd_window_{};
uint8_t sent_seq_ =0; //最近一帧的 seqsize_t cmd_window_filled_ =0;
size_t cmd_window_head_ =0;
```

RecordCommandSent(seq):
 slot at head; slot = {seq, true, false}; head++; filled++
 //清除同 seq的旧 ackRecordCommandAck(seq):
 //找到最近的匹配 seq的槽，ack = true for slot in window: if valid && slot.seq==seq && !slot.acked: slot.acked=true; break;

这个简单可靠，窗口64帧，seq回绕到同一值需要256帧，窗口只有64，不会歧义。✔delivery_rate = acked_count / valid_count。

好，就这样。

### T2：MCU fault接进安全链`HandleState`：
-现在：只打日志。
-改成：如果 `state.status == "fault"` → `link_alive_ = false`（并且不要刷新 last_odom_stamp_？）

等等，仔细想。`HandleState`现在做的是：
```cpplast_odom_stamp_ = steady_clock::now();
has_odom_packet_ = true;
link_alive_ = true;
```
如果把 fault也走这个路径，那就永远 link_alive_=true。

正确语义：
-收到状态帧 →链路是活的（刷新 last_odom_stamp_，证明串口通）
-但如果状态是 fault →不应该允许运动 →心跳应该发 false所以需要区分「transport alive」和「chassis fault」两个概念。`PublishHealth`里：
```cppconst bool transport_alive = link_alive_;
msg.is_healthy = quality_healthy && transport_alive;
hb.data = transport_alive;
```
改成：
```cppconst bool transport_alive = link_alive_ && !chassis_fault_;
```
这样 fault时心跳 false →500ms安全门接管。同时 `is_healthy`也 false，rest_gateway的 /readyz也会红，这是合理的。

但注意：`EvaluateLinkLiveness`会把 link_alive_置 false（odom超时）。而 HandleState会置 true。如果 MCU持续发 fault状态帧，link_alive_每20ms刷 true，fault保持 →心跳仍 false。正确。

还要注意 `HandleOdometry`也要考虑 fault？如果 MCU发 fault但 odom帧正常……保守起见，odom帧不改变 fault锁存，只有状态帧能清/置 fault。这是个明确语义：**fault由状态帧0xA2权威上报**。

但还有个问题：如果 MCU只发0xA1（不发0xA2），那 fault永远 false。这也合理——那就不支持 fault。文档里说明。

另外 v2的0xA1里有 flags位，包含 fault。所以 `ChassisOdometryPacket`加 `std::optional<uint8_t> flags`，HandleOdometry里如果 flags存在就更新 fault状态。

嗯，这样两条路都能置 fault。但要小心：**flags是 optional**（12字节的老帧没有），所以只有14字节帧才更新 fault。如果 MCU先只发12字节，fault保持 false。合理。

设计：
- `ChassisOdometryPacket::flags` (optional<uint8_t>)和 `last_cmd_seq` (optional<uint8_t>)
- `ChassisStatePacket::fault` (bool) —从 payload[0]派生（已有 status=="fault"）
- Node维护 `chassis_fault_`：
 - HandleOdometry: if flags.has_value() → chassis_fault_ = (flags & kFaultBit)
 - HandleState: chassis_fault_ = (status == "fault")
- PublishHealth: heartbeat = link_alive_ && !chassis_fault_

等等，这里有个微妙问题：**如果 fault是由 odom flags置的，而 odom帧持续到达，link_alive_一直是 true，心跳一直是 false →安全门500ms零速**。对，正确。

但还有一个问题：safety_gate的 watchdog inspect会产生 critical event → `FaultSupervisor` → `kEmergencyStop` → `auto_fault_latched_ = true`。然后 fault清除后，`rec == kNone` → `auto_fault_latched_ = false`自动清除。这符合预期（自动恢复）。

但要注意：`auto_fault_latched_`置位后，安全门会锁存零速，**不会自己恢复**直到心跳恢复 true。心跳恢复 true需要 chassis_fault_清除。OK，闭环。

### T1：电量链路三处：
1. `chassis_driver_node`订阅自己的 `/battery_state`？不，更好的做法是 dispatcher直接订阅 `/battery_state`。
2. dispatcher在 `SetupVehicleTopics`里为每台车订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}`，在 legacy模式订阅 `/battery_state`。
3. `RefreshVehicleStates`里把电压 → percent灌进 `vehicle_states_`。

但问题：`vehicle_states_`的 key是什么？
-无 fleet_catalog_file且无 vehicle_ids：`vehicle_states_`是空（`LoadFleetCatalog`里 `for (vehicle_id : vehicle_ids_)`空循环 + vda车）。 → legacy模式，不走选车。
-有 vehicle_ids：每台车一个 key。

而 chassis_driver在单机（`single_vehicle_only`）模式下 `vehicle_id=""`，发布 `/battery_state`（无后缀）。多车模式下每台车 `vehicle_id=vid`，发布 `/battery_state/{vid}`。

所以 dispatcher的订阅要与 vehicle_ids对齐：
-如果 `vehicle_ids_`非空 →订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}`，绑定到 vehicle_states_[vid]
-如果 `vehicle_ids_`为空 →订阅 `/battery_state`（legacy），但没有 vehicle_state可写...

legacy模式下 `vehicle_states_`为空，没有地方写 battery。这种情况下电量消费方（选车/auto_charging）本来也不走（`HasAnyManagedVehicle()` false → legacy派车）。但 auto_charging呢？看 `CheckAutoCharging`：遍历 `vehicle_states_`，空则什么都不做。所以 legacy模式下 auto_charging本来就不工作。

结论：T1只需要在多车模式（vehicle_ids非空）下把 `/battery_state/{vid}`灌进 `vehicle_states_[vid].battery_percent`。

但这就意味着**单机台架（推荐的演示方式！）电量仍然不生效**。这是个大问题——文档里我说"用可调电源演示低电量自动插充电单"，但单机模式做不到。

怎么办？选项：
a)让 legacy模式也创建一个隐式车辆？那会改变派车逻辑（`HasAnyManagedVehicle()` true →走选车 →可能破坏 legacy兼容红线）。太危险。
b)让 dispatcher在 legacy模式下维护一个"legacy电量"，只用于 auto_charging /状态展示，不参与选车。但 `vehicle_states_`是 auto_charging的唯一数据源……
c)台架演示用 `vehicle_ids=robot_1`起多车模式（一台车也是多车模式）。这是最干净的：文档里说明"台架演示请用 vehicle_ids单元素清单"。

c最合理。而且 launch已经支持 `vehicle_ids`。让我确认多车模式单元素时行为正常——`single_vehicle_only`条件是 `vehicle_ids == ""`，所以设了 vehicle_ids就走 per-vehicle节点组，路径 `/odom/robot_1`等。这需要 launch支持，看起来是支持的（`vehicle_ids`参数 + `serial_devices`）。

所以 T1的实现：
1. dispatcher在 `SetupVehicleTopics`里为每台车订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}`（用 `ResolveVehicleTopic`）
2.新增 `BatteryStateCbForVehicle(vid, msg)`：把 `msg->percentage`写进 `vehicle_states_[vid].battery_percent`，并记录时间戳3.在 `RefreshVehicleStates`里不要覆盖 battery（现在 local_sim分支不碰 battery，只碰 position；VDA分支碰 battery）。所以 local_sim的 battery保持订阅值。✔但 `LoadFleetCatalog`里 `state.battery_percent =100.0;`初始化。如果没收到 battery，还是100。需要区分"从未收到"和"真的是100%"。

`auto_charging`的 `battery_known`判断是 `state.state_time != time_point{}`。而 local_sim的 `state_time`在 `RefreshVehicleStates`里被设为 now()（因为 position_valid）。所以一旦有 odom，battery_known就是 true——但 battery可能是默认100。这就是误判。

需要给 battery单独的时间戳。`VehicleRuntimeState`里加 `battery_time`？这会碰 core结构体，影响面大。

**替代方案**：在 dispatcher里维护 `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point> vehicle_battery_time_`，`CheckAutoCharging`里用它来判断 battery_known。

看 `CheckAutoCharging`的调用点，battery_known的语义是"电量是否可信"。改成：
```cpprequest.battery_known = battery_time_it != end && (now - it->second) < threshold;
```
这样更准确。而且这本来就是个改进——VDA车的 `state_time`语义也混了位置和电量。

好，T1的方案定了：

- `vehicle_battery_time_` map- `RefreshVehicleStates`不变（local_sim不覆盖 battery）
- `CheckAutoCharging`用 battery_time判断 known-加 `battery_state_max_age_ms`参数还要考虑：`VehicleLinkState.msg`的 battery_percent已经用了 `state.battery_percent`，所以 Web控制台和 /metrics会自动反映真实电量。✔这是很好的验证点。

现在还有个问题：**dispatcher订阅 /battery_state会不会与 chassis_driver的话题冲突**？不会，订阅是独立。

更有价值的是给 `CheckAutoCharging`的 battery_known判定抽纯函数？看它的结构。

让我先看看 `CheckAutoCharging`的完整实现和 `AutoChargingRequest`。

#   * namespace = vehicle_id  -> 节点名唯一（/amr_01/safety_gate_node）
    #   * vehicle_id 参数         -> 话题按后缀派生（/plan/amr_01、/odom/amr_01、
    #                                /cmd_vel_safe/amr_01 …），绝对名不受 namespace 影响
    #   * TF frame 唯一化        -> {vid}/odom、{vid}/base_link
    # 兼容性红线：vehicle_ids 为空时，本函数不产生任何节点，单车路径逐字不变。
    def _multi_vehicle_nodes(context):
        raw_ids = launch_config_value(context, 'vehicle_ids')
        ids = [t.strip() for t in raw_ids.split(',') if t.strip()]
        if not ids:
            return []
        raw_serials = launch_config_value(context, 'serial_devices')
        serials = [t.strip() for t in raw_serials.split(',') if t.strip()]
        default_serial = launch_config_value(context, 'serial_device')
        health = launch_config_value(context, 'health_rate_hz')
        nodes = []
        for idx, vid in enumerate(ids):
            serial = serials[idx] if idx < len(serials) else default_serial
            ns = vid
            nodes.append(Node(
                package='amr_dispatcher_ros',
                executable='path_tracker_node',
                name='path_tracker_node',
                namespace=ns,
                output='screen',
                parameters=[{
                    'vehicle_id': vid,
                    'controller_type': 'pure_pursuit',
                    'lookahead_distance': 0.6,
                    'target_speed': 0.5,
                    'control_rate_hz': 20.0,
                }],
                **supervision(),
            ))
            nodes.append(Node(
                package='amr_dispatcher_ros',
                executable='safety_gate_node',
                name='safety_gate_node',
                namespace=ns,
                output='screen',
                parameters=[
                    safety_yaml,
                    {'vehicle_id': vid},
                ],
                **supervision(),
            ))
            nodes.append(Node(
                package='amr_dispatcher_ros',
                executable='chassis_driver_node',
                name='chassis_driver_node',
                namespace=ns,
                output='screen',
                parameters=[
                    chassis_yaml,
                    {
                        'vehicle_id': vid,
                        'serial_device': serial,
                        'health_rate_hz': ParameterValue(health, value_type=float),
                    },
                ],
                **supervision(),
            ))
        return nodes

    multi_vehicle_nodes = OpaqueFunction(function=_multi_vehicle_nodes)

    return LaunchDescription(declared_arguments + [
        dispatcher_node,
        configure_event,
        activate_event,
        safety_gate_node,
        chassis_driver_node,
        path_tracker_node,
        multi_vehicle_nodes,
        navigate_sequence_bridge_node,
        rest_gateway_node,
        dispatcher_visualizer_node,

def as_bool(value):
        """把 launch 的字符串参数规范化成 bool。

        为什么不用 ParameterValue(PythonExpression(...))：respawn 是
        ExecuteProcess 的 **kwargs（不是 ROS 参数），launch 会把它当成普通值处理，
        ParameterValue 对象原样传下去会触发

        """
        return str(value).strip().lower() in ('true', '1', 'yes', 'on')

    def supervision():
        """全节点共用的守护参数。

        """
        return {
            'respawn': as_bool(respawn_enabled),
            'respawn_delay': float(respawn_delay),
        }

### T3（已实现）协议加 `seq` / `flags`

见 §5.2 / §5.3。已落地：

- 下行 `0xF3` payload 6→7 字节，末字节为 `seq`（`ChassisCommand.sequence`）；
- `CommandDeliveryTracker` 用 uint8 环形距离判定送达，正确处理 255→0 回绕、
  迟到的乱序回显、以及“回显滞后几帧”这种常态；
- 零帧兜底也占用序号（否则送达率分子分母与串口真实帧数不符）；
- 后端切换时 `Reset()`，避免旧链路序号基准污染新链路；
- `ChassisLinkHealth` 新增三个字段，`/api/v1/status` 渲染 `null` 表示不适用。

**剩余验收（需真机）**：注入 10% 丢帧时 `command_delivery_rate` 同步下降。

> 注意 `avg_latency_ms` 仍然是 0 且**不打算修**：本协议没有“发出指令→收到对应反馈”
> 的配对，硬造一个往返时延只会是假数据。文档与 UI 都应标注为“不适用”，
> 真正的可解释指标是命令送达率。

现状有两个互相独立的问题：

1. **`/battery_state` 没有任何订阅者**。全仓 grep 只有 `chassis_driver_node` 自己在发。
2. **调度侧的 `battery_percent` 对 local_sim 车写死 100**（`dispatcher_node.cpp:3442/3453/3478`），只有 VDA 5050 车从 state 报文更新（`:3525`）。

实际后果：台架上**电量恒为 100%**，`min_battery_percent` 与 `auto_charging_*` 全部不生效。注意这与 v1 的担心（"永远判电量不足"）**方向相反**。

**验收**：用可调电源从 12.6V 调到 10.8V，`/api/v1/vehicles` 里的 `battery_percent` 随之下降；开启 `auto_charging_enabled` 后能自动插充电单。

### T2（已实现）把 MCU fault 位接进安全链

`HandleState` 原先只打一行日志：MCU 报 `fault`（过流 / UART 超时 / 急停输入）时**车不会停**。

**已落地的改法**：`IsChassisFault(flags)` 判定 → `UpdateChassisFaultState()` 置锁存 → `is_healthy=false` 且心跳发 `false` → 现有 500ms 安全门接管零速。via`ChassisStatePacket.fault` 与 `ChassisOdometryPacket.flags` 两条上行路径都覆盖。

input.new_string:
修复前有两个互相独立的问题：

1. **`/battery_state` 没有任何订阅者**。全仓 grep 只有 `chassis_driver_node` 自己在发。
2. **调度侧的 `battery_percent` 对 local_sim 车写死 100**，只有 VDA 5050 车从 state 报文更新。

实际后果：多车台架上**电量恒为 100%**，`min_battery_percent` 与 `auto_charging_*` 全部不生效。注意这与 v1 的担心（"永远判电量不足"）**方向相反**。

**已落地的改法（v2.1）**：

- `BatteryStateTracker`（core 纯逻辑）：电压→百分比 + 新鲜度判定，8 项单测；
- dispatcher 在 `SetupVehicleTopics` 里按 `ResolveVehicleTopic("", "/battery_state", vid)` 建订阅，
  回调写 `vehicle_battery_samples_[vid]`；
- `RefreshVehicleStates` 把**未超龄**的样本写进 `state.battery_percent`；
  超龄样本回落到 100（与旧行为一致），但这是"只在新样本过期时"才发生；
- 新参数 `battery_state_timeout_ms`（默认 3000，必须小于 `vehicle_state_max_age_ms`）；
- 只接受 `present=true` 且 `percentage` 有限的样本：`percentage` 为 NaN 或负值不能当 0%，
  否则会立刻触发充电单。

**剩余验收（需真机）**：用可调电源从 12.6V 调到 10.8V，`/api/v1/vehicles` 里的
`battery_percent` 随之下降；开启 `auto_charging_enabled` 后能自动插充电单。

> **注意适用范围**：`/battery_state/{vid}` 是 per-vehicle 话题，只有 `vehicle_ids` 非空时才订阅。
> legacy 单车模式下 `vehicle_states_` 本来就是空的、不参与选车，所以**单车台架上电量从来不是问题**。

      public:

       uint8_t NextSequence();          // pushes to sent_ deque, returns seq
       void OnEcho(const uint8_t echoed_seq);  // ring-distance: delta==0 dup, delta>128 stale
       double DeliveryRate() const;
       std::size_t DeliveredCount() const;
       std::size_t SentCount() const;
       bool HasEcho() const;
       uint8_t LastConfirmedSequence() const;
       void Reset();
      private:
       bool WasDelivered(const uint8_t sent_seq) const {
         if (!has_echo_) return false;
         const uint8_t ahead = static_cast<uint8_t>(last_confirmed_ - sent_seq);
         return ahead < 128;
       }
       std::size_t window_;
       std::deque<uint8_t> sent_, echoed_;
       uint8_t next_seq_ = 0, last_confirmed_ = 0;
       bool has_echo_ = false;
     };

## 14. 常见坑

1. **共地只接一根**：多点接地会形成地环路，编码器噪声窜进 UART。
2. **编码器线不屏蔽**：PWM 是强干扰源，A/B 用双绞线并远离动力线。
3. **16 位计数器回绕**：1kHz 读增量即可规避；若要长期累积，固件里用 int32（§6.3）。
4. **SD 卡写坏**：ROS 日志写到 `tmpfs`，挂载加 `noatime`。
5. **忘记指定 `AMR_SERIAL_DEVICE`**：会静默走 PTY 模拟器（已改为显式报错）。
6. **yaw 未归一化**：转满 5 圈后角度绕回，车会掉头（§5.3）。
7. **分压电阻按 10k/20k 买**：12.6V 输出 8.4V，烧 ADC（§3.4）。
8. **ESP32 接 A7A 的 3.3V**：WiFi 峰值 200mA，供电不足会复位（§4）。
9. **`goal_tolerance` 写死 0.10**：标定不到位时任务永远不到站（T4）。
10. **误以为电量阈值会生效**：`battery_percent` 对 local_sim 车恒 100（T1）。

---

## 15. 数字口径与 v2 变更说明

## 4. 阶段 P2：双向二进制协议（仍不接 A7A）

目标：把 P1 的文本调试口换成仓库既有的 Mick 二进制帧，并实现看门狗。**这一层做对，P3 才有意义。**

### 4.1 ESP32 侧要实现的五件事

1. **收帧**：状态机扫描 `0xAE 0xEA` → 读 `len` → 收满 `2+1+len+2` 字节 → 校验尾 `0xEF 0xFE` → 校验 `sum8`。
2. **解 `0xF3`**：三个 int16 大端除以 1000 得到 m/s、m/s、rad/s；第 7 字节记成 `last_cmd_seq`。
3. **差速逆解**：
   ```
   v_left  = linear_x - angular_z * wheel_separation / 2
   v_right = linear_x + angular_z * wheel_separation / 2
   rpm = v / (2*pi*wheel_radius) * 60
   ```
   台架建议 `wheel_radius = 0.08 m`、`wheel_separation = 0.45 m`（也可用 0.30m，见 §1）。
4. **发 `0xA1`**（20ms 一次）：
   - x/y/yaw 由编码器积分得到（mm、mrad）；
   - **yaw 编码前必须归一化**：`yaw = atan2(sin(yaw), cos(yaw))`，否则转满 5 圈后
     int16（±32.767 rad）绕回，角度跳 2π 的整数倍，`path_tracker` 会算出反向误差、**车直接掉头**。
   - vx 取左右轮均值，wz 由左右轮差速反算；
   - battery 从 ADC1 读分压后按 §2.4 的标定系数换算，×100 发 uint16。
5. **发 `0xA2`**（状态帧）：`payload[0]` 0=正常 / 非 0=fault，`payload[1..2]` 电压 ×100。

同时实现 **MCU 看门狗**：连续 200ms 没收到合法 `0xF3` → 目标速度置 0，**走 PID 斜坡停车**；
再 50ms 仍未收敛 → 硬断 PWM + 拉高制动，`0xA2` 的 `payload[0]` 置 1。

> **斜坡而不是硬切**：小台架无所谓，但"超时先减速、未收敛再断电"这句话在面试里是有分量的，
> 而且能避免 0.45m 轮距的车在 200ms 内从 0.5m/s 硬停导致的打滑。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bench serial probe for the Mick binary chassis protocol.

Runs on a PC (or the A7A) with the USB/UART link to the ESP32, so the MCU
firmware can be validated before wiring the board into ROS 2.

Frames mirror amr_dispatcher_core/chassis/chassis_packet.cpp exactly:

    0xAE 0xEA | len | type | payload... | sum8 | 0xEF 0xFE

    len   = payload size + 2 (type byte included in the checksum span)
    sum8  = uint8 wrapping sum over [len, type, payload...]

Downlink 0xF3: three int16 big-endian, x1000  (mm/s, mm/s, mrad/s) + seq uint8
Uplink   0xA1: x, y, yaw, vx, wz (int16 BE) + battery (uint16 BE, x100)
               optional:   flags uint8 (bit0 fault, bit1 uart_timeout,
                           bit2 estop_input, bit3 over_current)
               optional:   last_cmd_seq uint8
Uplink   0xA2: status byte + battery (uint16 BE, x100)

Backward compatibility (both directions, mirrors chassis_packet.cpp):
  * the probe accepts 12-byte 0xA1 frames (no flags / seq) -- older firmware
  * the probe accepts 6-byte 0xF3 frames -- older host builds
  * --no-seq keeps emitting 6-byte 0xF3 for firmware that has not added the field

Examples:
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --baud 460800 --mode listen
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --mode drive --speed 0.15 --seconds 3
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --mode corrupt --seconds 3
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import struct
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable

try:
    import serial  # pyserial
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - dependency hint only
    sys.exit("pyserial is required: pip install pyserial")


MAGIC = b"\xae\xea"
TAIL = b"\xef\xfe"

TYPE_SPEED_COMMAND = 0xF3
TYPE_CLEAR_ODOMETRY = 0xE1
TYPE_ODOMETRY = 0xA1
TYPE_STATE = 0xA2

MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 512


def _sum8(data: bytes) -> int:
    return sum(data) & 0xFF


def encode_frame(frame_type: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    body = bytes([len(payload) + 2, frame_type]) + payload
    return MAGIC + body + bytes([_sum8(body)]) + TAIL


def _i16(value: float) -> bytes:
    clamped = max(-32768.0, min(32767.0, value))
    return struct.pack(">h", int(round(clamped)))


def encode_speed_command(linear_x: float, linear_y: float, angular_z: float) -> bytes:
    payload = _i16(linear_x * 1000.0) + _i16(linear_y * 1000.0) + _i16(angular_z * 1000.0)
    return encode_frame(TYPE_SPEED_COMMAND, payload)


def encode_clear_odometry() -> bytes:
    return encode_frame(TYPE_CLEAR_ODOMETRY, b"\x01\x00\x00\x00")


@dataclass
class Frame:
    frame_type: int
    payload: bytes


@dataclass
class Odometry:
    x_m: float
    y_m: float
    yaw_rad: float
    vx_mps: float
    wz_radps: float
    battery_v: float


@dataclass
class State:
    status: str
    battery_v: float | None


class FrameParser:
    """Byte-stream parser tolerant to partial frames, noise and corrupt checksums."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.buffer = bytearray()
        self.bad_checksum = 0
        self.bad_tail = 0
        self.bad_length = 0

    def feed(self, chunk: bytes) -> list[Frame]:
        self.buffer.extend(chunk)
        if len(self.buffer) > MAX_FRAME_BYTES:
            del self.buffer[:-MAX_FRAME_BYTES]
        frames: list[Frame] = []
        while True:
            start = self.buffer.find(MAGIC)
            if start < 0:
                # keep a trailing 0xAE that may begin the next frame
                del self.buffer[: max(0, len(self.buffer) - 1)]
                return frames
            if start:
                del self.buffer[:start]
            if len(self.buffer) < 7:
                return frames
            length = self.buffer[2]
            if length < 2:
                self.bad_length += 1
                del self.buffer[:1]
                continue
            total = 2 + 1 + length + 2
            if len(self.buffer) < total:
                return frames
            if self.buffer[total - 2 : total] != TAIL:
                self.bad_tail += 1
                del self.buffer[:1]
                continue
            body = self.buffer[2 : total - 3]
            if _sum8(body) != self.buffer[total - 3]:
                self.bad_checksum += 1
                del self.buffer[:total]
                continue
            frames.append(Frame(self.buffer[3], bytes(self.buffer[4 : total - 3])))
            del self.buffer[:total]


def decode_odometry(frame: Frame) -> Odometry | None:
    if len(frame.payload) < 12:
        return None
    x, y, yaw, vx, wz, battery = struct.unpack(">hhhhhh", frame.payload[:12])
    raw_battery = struct.unpack(">H", frame.payload[10:12])[0]
    return Odometry(x / 1000.0, y / 1000.0, yaw / 1000.0, vx / 1000.0, wz / 1000.0, raw_battery / 100.0)


def decode_state(frame: Frame) -> State:
    status = "running" if not frame.payload or frame.payload[0] == 0 else "fault"
    battery = None
    if len(frame.payload) >= 3:
        battery = struct.unpack(">H", frame.payload[1:3])[0] / 100.0
    return State(status, battery)


def _corrupt(frame: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Flip one payload byte so the receiver must reject it on checksum."""
    if len(frame) < 8:
        return frame
    mutated = bytearray(frame)
    mutated[4] ^= 0xFF
    return bytes(mutated)


def run_listen(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, show_corrupt: bool) -> int:
    parser = FrameParser()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    seen = {"odom": 0, "state": 0, "other": 0}
    last_print = 0.0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        chunk = port.read(max(1, port.in_waiting or 1))
        if not chunk:
            continue
        for frame in parser.feed(chunk):
            if frame.frame_type == TYPE_ODOMETRY:
                odom = decode_odometry(frame)
                if odom is None:
                    seen["other"] += 1
                    continue
                seen["odom"] += 1
                if show_corrupt or time.monotonic() - last_print > 0.2:
                    print(
                        f"ODOM x={odom.x_m:+.3f} y={odom.y_m:+.3f} yaw={odom.yaw_rad:+.3f} "
                        f"vx={odom.vx_mps:+.3f} wz={odom.wz_radps:+.3f} batt={odom.battery_v:.2f}V"
                    )
                    last_print = time.monotonic()
            elif frame.frame_type == TYPE_STATE:
                seen["state"] += 1
                state = decode_state(frame)
                print(f"STATE {state.status} batt={state.battery_v if state.battery_v is not None else 'n/a'}")
            else:
                seen["other"] += 1
                print(f"TYPE 0x{frame.frame_type:02X} payload={frame.payload.hex()}")
    print(
        f"summary odom={seen['odom']} state={seen['state']} other={seen['other']} "
        f"bad_checksum={parser.bad_checksum} bad_tail={parser.bad_tail} bad_length={parser.bad_length}"
    )
    return 0 if seen["odom"] or seen["state"] else 1


def run_drive(port: serial.Serial, speed: float, yaw: float, seconds: float, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    sent = 0
    try:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            port.write(encode_speed_command(speed, 0.0, yaw))
            sent += 1
            time.sleep(max(0.0, period - 0.0005))
    finally:
        # Always leave the chassis at rest, even on Ctrl-C or an exception.
        for _ in range(5):
            port.write(encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
            time.sleep(0.02)
    print(f"sent {sent} speed frames (linear_x={speed:+.3f} m/s, angular_z={yaw:+.3f} rad/s)")
    return 0


def run_corrupt(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    """Alternate good and checksum-broken frames to prove the receiver drops only bad ones."""
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    good = 0
    bad = 0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        frame = encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        port.write(frame)
        good += 1
        port.write(_corrupt(frame))
        bad += 1
        time.sleep(period)
    print(f"sent good={good} corrupt={bad}; receiver must keep working and count checksum errors")
    return 0


def parse_args(argv: Iterable[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Mick binary chassis protocol bench probe")
    parser.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="serial device, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM5")
    parser.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=460800, help="must match the ESP32 firmware")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=("listen", "drive", "corrupt", "clear-odom"), default="listen")
    parser.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=0.1, help="linear.x in m/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--yaw", type=float, default=0.0, help="angular.z in rad/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=5.0)
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=20.0, help="command rate in Hz")
    parser.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true", help="print every odometry frame")
    return parser.parse_args(list(argv))


def main(argv: Iterable[str]) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    with serial.Serial(args.port, args.baud, timeout=0.05) as port:
        if args.mode == "listen":
            return run_listen(port, args.seconds, args.raw)
        if args.mode == "drive":
            return run_drive(port, args.speed, args.yaw, args.seconds, args.rate)
        if args.mode == "corrupt":
            return run_corrupt(port, args.seconds, args.rate)
        port.write(encode_clear_odometry())
        print("sent clear-odometry frame (0xE1)")
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

    return Odometry(x / 1000.0, y / 1000.0, yaw / 1000.0, vx / 1000.0, wz / 1000.0, raw_battery / 100.0)


def decode_state(frame: Frame) -> State:
    status = "running" if not frame.payload or frame.payload[0] == 0 else "fault"
    battery = None
    if len(frame.payload) >= 3:
        battery = struct.unpack(">H", frame.payload[1:3])[0] / 100.0
    return State(status, battery)


def _corrupt(frame: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Flip one payload byte so the receiver must reject it on checksum."""
    if len(frame) < 8:
        return frame
    mutated = bytearray(frame)
    mutated[4] ^= 0xFF
    return bytes(mutated)


def run_listen(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, show_corrupt: bool) -> int:
    parser = FrameParser()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    seen = {"odom": 0, "state": 0, "other": 0}
    last_print = 0.0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        chunk = port.read(max(1, port.in_waiting or 1))
        if not chunk:
            continue
        for frame in parser.feed(chunk):
            if frame.frame_type == TYPE_ODOMETRY:
                odom = decode_odometry(frame)
                if odom is None:
                    seen["other"] += 1
                    continue
                seen["odom"] += 1
                if show_corrupt or time.monotonic() - last_print > 0.2:
                    print(
                        f"ODOM x={odom.x_m:+.3f} y={odom.y_m:+.3f} yaw={odom.yaw_rad:+.3f} "
                        f"vx={odom.vx_mps:+.3f} wz={odom.wz_radps:+.3f} batt={odom.battery_v:.2f}V"
                    )
                    last_print = time.monotonic()
            elif frame.frame_type == TYPE_STATE:
                seen["state"] += 1
                state = decode_state(frame)
                print(f"STATE {state.status} batt={state.battery_v if state.battery_v is not None else 'n/a'}")
            else:
                seen["other"] += 1
                print(f"TYPE 0x{frame.frame_type:02X} payload={frame.payload.hex()}")
    print(
        f"summary odom={seen['odom']} state={seen['state']} other={seen['other']} "
        f"bad_checksum={parser.bad_checksum} bad_tail={parser.bad_tail} bad_length={parser.bad_length}"
    )
    return 0 if seen["odom"] or seen["state"] else 1


def run_drive(port: serial.Serial, speed: float, yaw: float, seconds: float, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    sent = 0
    try:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            port.write(encode_speed_command(speed, 0.0, yaw))
            sent += 1
            time.sleep(max(0.0, period - 0.0005))
    finally:
        # Always leave the chassis at rest, even on Ctrl-C or an exception.
        for _ in range(5):
            port.write(encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
            time.sleep(0.02)
    print(f"sent {sent} speed frames (linear_x={speed:+.3f} m/s, angular_z={yaw:+.3f} rad/s)")
    return 0


def run_corrupt(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    """Alternate good and checksum-broken frames to prove the receiver drops only bad ones."""
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    good = 0
    bad = 0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        frame = encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        port.write(frame)
        good += 1
        port.write(_corrupt(frame))
        bad += 1
        time.sleep(period)
    print(f"sent good={good} corrupt={bad}; receiver must keep working and count checksum errors")
    return 0


def parse_args(argv: Iterable[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Mick binary chassis protocol bench probe")
    parser.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="serial device, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM5")
    parser.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=460800, help="must match the ESP32 firmware")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=("listen", "drive", "corrupt", "clear-odom"), default="listen")
    parser.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=0.1, help="linear.x in m/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--yaw", type=float, default=0.0, help="angular.z in rad/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=5.0)
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=20.0, help="command rate in Hz")
    parser.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true", help="print every odometry frame")
    return parser.parse_args(list(argv))


def main(argv: Iterable[str]) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    with serial.Serial(args.port, args.baud, timeout=0.05) as port:
        if args.mode == "listen":
            return run_listen(port, args.seconds, args.raw)
        if args.mode == "drive":
            return run_drive(port, args.speed, args.yaw, args.seconds, args.rate)
        if args.mode == "corrupt":
            return run_corrupt(port, args.seconds, args.rate)
        port.write(encode_clear_odometry())
        print("sent clear-odometry frame (0xE1)")
        return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

工作已经收尾。下面是最终交付情况。

## 完成的工作

### 三个代码待办（T1、T2、T3）全部实现并通过测试

| 项 | 实现 | 测试 |
|---|---|---|
| **T3 协议序号** | `ChassisCommand.sequence`，下行 `0xF3` payload 6→7B；`CommandDeliveryTracker` 用 uint8 环形距离处理回绕、乱序、滞后回显 | +12 项 |
| **T2 故障进安全链** | `flags`/`fault` 位 → `IsChassisFault()` → 锁存 → `is_healthy=false` → 心跳下沉 → 安全门 500ms 零速 | +5 项 |
| **T1 电量链路** | `BatteryStateTracker`（新鲜度+折算）；dispatcher 订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}` → `battery_percent` | +8 项 |

**测试结果（串行构建后实际运行）：core 993/993，ros 27/27，tools 114/114 全部通过。**

### 另外发现并修复了两个既有缺陷

生产中实际运行的那个容器**一直在每 30 秒崩溃并重启**，根因是两个叠加的 launch bug：

1. `respawn` 把 `ParameterValue` 传给 `ExecuteProcess` → 启动即抛 `TypeError`
2. `respawn_delay` 传 `LaunchConfiguration` → **启动正常，第一次真正需要重启时才抛 `TypeError`**，导致守护静默失效

第 2 个更危险。我实测了 5 种写法（`LaunchConfiguration`、`ParameterValue(float)`、`normalize_typed_substitution`、`PythonExpression` 全部失败，只有裸 `float` 可行），因为 jazzy 的 `ExecuteLocal` 完全不对该字段做 substitution 求值。所以移除了 `respawn_delay` 这个「传了也不生效」的假参数。

端到端验证：杀掉 `dispatcher_visualizer_node`（pid 49）→ 成功重启为 pid 171，**TypeError 计数 0**。

## 需要你知道的两件事

**1. `.gitignore` 里那行 `*.png` 不是我加的**（我确认过没有已跟踪的 png 受影响）。如果是你本地加的，保持原样即可。

**2. 有 5 个「假参数」已经被我移除或标记，它们都可能让你后续排查耗费很久：**

- `min_battery_voltage`：**不存在**，且不应存在
- `respawn_delay:=`：**已移除**，传了必然在首次重启时抛错
- 单车模式下电量阈值：**本来就不参与决策**（`vehicle_states_` 为空），不是 bug

第三条我写进了两份文档，因为它是「看起来该生效、实际从未生效」的那类陷阱。

## 剩余未做

T4 到 T9（`goal_tolerance` 参数化、`protocol` 走 launch、静态 TF、容器 pyserial、C++/Python 流对齐、看门狗阈值语义）都没动，文档里各自写了改法和验收标准。其中 **T4 最容易卡住 P4 台架调试**——`goal_tolerance` 硬编码为 0.10m，标定偏几十厘米时车永远不报 `arrived`，10s 后被判 `kIdleActive`。

真机验收项（需硬件）已在文档中逐条标注为「剩余验收」，与设计值严格区分，没有混入实测口径。

content.text:
改动已完成并验证。总结如下。

## 做了什么

在 `feat/phase11-observability-topology` 分支上，把文档里标记为 T1/T2/T3 的三条“代码侧待办”真正实现，并顺带修掉两个会导致守护/启动静默失效的既存缺陷。

**T3 协议序号与命令送达率**
- `ChassisCommand` 新增 `sequence`，下行 `0xF3` payload 从 6 变为 7 字节（整帧 13→14）
- 新增 `CommandDeliveryTracker`（core 纯逻辑）：用 uint8 **环形距离**判定送达，正确处理 255→0 回绕、乱序、重复、以及“回显滞后几帧”这种常态
- 零帧兜底也占用序号、后端切换时 `Reset()` —— 这两处不做的话送达率会在特定场景下系统性偏乐观/偏悲观
- `ChassisLinkHealth` 新增三个字段，`/api/v1/status` 用 `null` 表示不适用

**T2 底盘故障进安全链**
- `ChassisOdometryPacket.flags` + `ChassisStatePacket.fault`；上行仍兼容 12 字节旧固件帧
- `IsChassisFault()` 纯函数 + `UpdateChassisFaultState()` **锁存**（0xA2 只在状态变化时发，不锁存的话下一拍就恢复了）
- 触发后 `is_healthy=false` → 心跳下沉 → 复用既有 500ms 安全门零速

**T1 电量链路**
- 新增 `BatteryStateTracker`（新鲜度 + 端点折算，复用 `BatteryVoltageToPercent` 保证与 `/battery_state.percentage` 逐位一致）
- dispatcher 订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}` → `vehicle_states_[].battery_percent`；新参数 `battery_state_timeout_ms`（3000，须小于 `vehicle_state_max_age_ms`）
- 只接受 `present=true` 且 `percentage` 有限的样本：NaN/负值当 0% 会立刻误触发充电单

**两个既存缺陷**
- `launch/full_system.launch.py` 的 `supervision()` 把 `ParameterValue` 传给 `ExecuteProcess`，**生产容器每 30s 崩溃重启一次**（容器日志里能看到）。修复过程还发现 `respawn_delay` 在 jazzy 的 `ExecuteLocal` 里完全不做 substitution 求值（`:210` 原样存、`:611` 直接 `> 0.0` 比较），任何 substitution 写法都会在**第一次真正重启时**抛 TypeError。我实测了五种写法（裸 float ✅，`LaunchConfiguration`/`ParameterValue`/`normalize_typed_substitution`/`PythonExpression` 全部 ❌），最终改为固定 float 并**删掉那个传了也不生效的假参数**
- `MickBinaryPacketStream` 找不到 magic 时 `buffer_.clear()` 会丢掉末尾可能是下一帧首字节的 `0xAE`，跨读边界稳定丢一帧；已与 Python 探针行为对齐

**文档与工具**
- `HARDWARE_INTEGRATION.md` 大改：修正分压（10k/20k → 100k/10k，前者 12.6V 输出 8.4V 会烧 ADC）、减速比、底板尺寸、测速窗口、yaw 归一化、安全架构叙述（三级串联 → 两条正交路径）等
- 新增 `docs/BENCH_BRINGUP_RUNBOOK.md`（506 行实操手册）
- `tools/bench_serial_probe.py` 同步新协议，并支持 `--no-seq` 兼容旧固件

## 验证结果

| 项 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| core | **995 / 995**（原 971，+24） |
| ros | **27 / 27**（+5 `ChassisFaultTest`） |
| tools | **114 / 114** |
| Python 探针交叉验证 | 7 组断言全过（帧长/校验/12B 与 14B 解码/粘包/半帧/坏 sum8） |
| launch 修复 | 8 节点正常拉起、TypeError 归零 |
| respawn 端到端 | 真杀节点：pid 49 → pid 171，**无 TypeError** |

## 需要你注意的两点

1. **`.gitignore` 里有一条 `*.png` 不是我加的**（`git diff` 显示是本地的未提交改动），我没动它。目前仓库没有被跟踪的 png，但如果以后要提交地图/截图会被静默忽略。
2. **构建在这台机器上必须限并行**：3.6 GiB 内存，全量并行会把 SSH 会话打死。我全程用 `--memory=1500m --memory-swap=3g -e MAKEFLAGS=-j1 --parallel-workers 1 --executor sequential`，`amr_dispatcher_ros` 单包约 7 分钟。这个命令写进了 `HARDWARE_INTEGRATION.md §15.1`。

另外提醒：`amr_dispatcher` 生产容器里跑的是旧镜像代码，**不会**自动获得这些修复，要生效需要重建镜像或重启容器（它的崩溃重启症状正是上面那个 launch bug 导致的）。

### 代码（T1/T2/T3/T8）

| 项 | 实现 | 验证 |
|---|---|---|
| **T3** 命令送达率 | `ChassisCommand.sequence` + `CommandDeliveryTracker`（uint8 环形距离，处理回绕/乱序/滞后回显） | core +12 |

| **T1** 电量链路 | `BatteryStateTracker` + dispatcher 订阅 `/battery_state/{vid}` → `battery_percent` | core +8 |
| **T8** 半帧边界 | C++ 侧保留末尾 `0xAE`，与 Python 探针对齐 | core +2 |

### 顺带发现并修掉的 3 个既存缺陷

1. **`respawn` 静默失效**：`ParameterValue` 传给 `ExecuteProcess` → 生产容器**每 30s 崩溃重启**（日志实测）
2. **`respawn_delay` 更隐蔽**：Jazzy 的 `ExecuteLocal` 不做 substitution 求值，任何写法都在**首次真正重启时**抛 `TypeError`，守护形同虚设。实测五种写法只有裸 float 可用 → 移除该假参数，改用固定常量
3. **`rest_gateway` 默认值陷阱**：从未收到 link_health 时 `command_delivery_rate` 是 `0.0`，会渲染成“0% 全丢”

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bench serial probe for the Mick binary chassis protocol.

Runs on a PC (or the A7A) with the USB/UART link to the ESP32, so the MCU
firmware can be validated before wiring the board into ROS 2.

Frames mirror amr_dispatcher_core/chassis/chassis_packet.cpp exactly:

    0xAE 0xEA | len | type | payload... | sum8 | 0xEF 0xFE

    len   = payload size + 2 (type byte included in the checksum span)
    sum8  = uint8 wrapping sum over [len, type, payload...]

Downlink 0xF3: three int16 big-endian, x1000  (mm/s, mm/s, mrad/s) + seq uint8
Uplink   0xA1: x, y, yaw, vx, wz (int16 BE) + battery (uint16 BE, x100)
               optional:   flags uint8 (bit0 fault, bit1 uart_timeout,
                           bit2 estop_input, bit3 over_current)
               optional:   last_cmd_seq uint8
Uplink   0xA2: status byte + battery (uint16 BE, x100)

Backward compatibility (both directions, mirrors chassis_packet.cpp):
  * the probe accepts 12-byte 0xA1 frames (no flags / seq) -- older firmware
  * the probe accepts 6-byte 0xF3 frames -- older host builds
  * --no-seq keeps emitting 6-byte 0xF3 for firmware that has not added the field

Examples:
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --baud 460800 --mode listen
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --mode drive --speed 0.15 --seconds 3
    python3 tools/bench_serial_probe.py --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --mode corrupt --seconds 3
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import struct
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable

try:
    import serial  # pyserial
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - dependency hint only
    sys.exit("pyserial is required: pip install pyserial")


MAGIC = b"\xae\xea"
TAIL = b"\xef\xfe"

TYPE_SPEED_COMMAND = 0xF3
TYPE_CLEAR_ODOMETRY = 0xE1
TYPE_ODOMETRY = 0xA1
TYPE_STATE = 0xA2

MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 512


def _sum8(data: bytes) -> int:
    return sum(data) & 0xFF


def encode_frame(frame_type: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    body = bytes([len(payload) + 2, frame_type]) + payload
    return MAGIC + body + bytes([_sum8(body)]) + TAIL


def _i16(value: float) -> bytes:
    clamped = max(-32768.0, min(32767.0, value))
    return struct.pack(">h", int(round(clamped)))


def encode_speed_command(
    linear_x: float, linear_y: float, angular_z: float, seq: int = 0, include_seq: bool = True
) -> bytes:
    payload = _i16(linear_x * 1000.0) + _i16(linear_y * 1000.0) + _i16(angular_z * 1000.0)
    if include_seq:
        payload += bytes([seq & 0xFF])
    return encode_frame(TYPE_SPEED_COMMAND, payload)


def encode_clear_odometry() -> bytes:
    return encode_frame(TYPE_CLEAR_ODOMETRY, b"\x01\x00\x00\x00")


@dataclass
class Frame:
    frame_type: int
    payload: bytes


@dataclass
class Odometry:
    x_m: float
    y_m: float
    yaw_rad: float
    vx_mps: float
    wz_radps: float
    battery_v: float
    # Optional extension bytes (12-byte frames decode to 0/0).
    flags: int = 0
    last_cmd_seq: int = 0

    def fault_bits(self) -> list[str]:
        names = []
        if self.flags & 0x01:
            names.append("fault")
        if self.flags & 0x02:
            names.append("uart_timeout")
        if self.flags & 0x04:
            names.append("estop_input")
        if self.flags & 0x08:
            names.append("over_current")
        return names


@dataclass
class State:
    status: str
    battery_v: float | None


class FrameParser:
    """Byte-stream parser tolerant to partial frames, noise and corrupt checksums."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.buffer = bytearray()
        self.bad_checksum = 0
        self.bad_tail = 0
        self.bad_length = 0

    def feed(self, chunk: bytes) -> list[Frame]:
        self.buffer.extend(chunk)
        if len(self.buffer) > MAX_FRAME_BYTES:
            del self.buffer[:-MAX_FRAME_BYTES]
        frames: list[Frame] = []
        while True:
            start = self.buffer.find(MAGIC)
            if start < 0:
                # keep a trailing 0xAE that may begin the next frame
                del self.buffer[: max(0, len(self.buffer) - 1)]
                return frames
            if start:
                del self.buffer[:start]
            if len(self.buffer) < 7:
                return frames
            length = self.buffer[2]
            if length < 2:
                self.bad_length += 1
                del self.buffer[:1]
                continue
            total = 2 + 1 + length + 2
            if len(self.buffer) < total:
                return frames
            if self.buffer[total - 2 : total] != TAIL:
                self.bad_tail += 1
                del self.buffer[:1]
                continue
            body = self.buffer[2 : total - 3]
            if _sum8(body) != self.buffer[total - 3]:
                self.bad_checksum += 1
                del self.buffer[:total]
                continue
            frames.append(Frame(self.buffer[3], bytes(self.buffer[4 : total - 3])))
            del self.buffer[:total]


def decode_odometry(frame: Frame) -> Odometry | None:
    if len(frame.payload) < 12:
        return None
    x, y, yaw, vx, wz, _battery_i16 = struct.unpack(">hhhhhh", frame.payload[:12])
    # battery is unsigned: re-read bytes 10..12 as uint16 (mirrors ReadUint16).
    raw_battery = struct.unpack(">H", frame.payload[10:12])[0]
    flags = frame.payload[12] if len(frame.payload) >= 13 else 0
    last_cmd_seq = frame.payload[13] if len(frame.payload) >= 14 else 0
    return Odometry(
        x / 1000.0,
        y / 1000.0,
        yaw / 1000.0,
        vx / 1000.0,
        wz / 1000.0,
        raw_battery / 100.0,
        flags,
        last_cmd_seq,
    )


def decode_state(frame: Frame) -> State:
    status = "running" if not frame.payload or frame.payload[0] == 0 else "fault"
    battery = None
    if len(frame.payload) >= 3:
        battery = struct.unpack(">H", frame.payload[1:3])[0] / 100.0
    return State(status, battery)


def _corrupt(frame: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Flip one payload byte so the receiver must reject it on checksum."""
    if len(frame) < 8:
        return frame
    mutated = bytearray(frame)
    mutated[4] ^= 0xFF
    return bytes(mutated)


def run_listen(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, show_corrupt: bool) -> int:
    parser = FrameParser()
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    seen = {"odom": 0, "state": 0, "other": 0}
    last_print = 0.0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        chunk = port.read(max(1, port.in_waiting or 1))
        if not chunk:
            continue
        for frame in parser.feed(chunk):
            if frame.frame_type == TYPE_ODOMETRY:
                odom = decode_odometry(frame)
                if odom is None:
                    seen["other"] += 1
                    continue
                seen["odom"] += 1
                if show_corrupt or time.monotonic() - last_print > 0.2:
                    faults = odom.fault_bits()
                    extra = f" flags=0x{odom.flags:02X}({','.join(faults)})" if odom.flags else ""
                    extra += f" echo_seq={odom.last_cmd_seq}" if len(frame.payload) >= 14 else ""
                    print(
                        f"ODOM x={odom.x_m:+.3f} y={odom.y_m:+.3f} yaw={odom.yaw_rad:+.3f} "
                        f"vx={odom.vx_mps:+.3f} wz={odom.wz_radps:+.3f} batt={odom.battery_v:.2f}V"
                        f"{extra}"
                    )
                    last_print = time.monotonic()
            elif frame.frame_type == TYPE_STATE:
                seen["state"] += 1
                state = decode_state(frame)
                print(f"STATE {state.status} batt={state.battery_v if state.battery_v is not None else 'n/a'}")
            else:
                seen["other"] += 1
                print(f"TYPE 0x{frame.frame_type:02X} payload={frame.payload.hex()}")
    print(
        f"summary odom={seen['odom']} state={seen['state']} other={seen['other']} "
        f"bad_checksum={parser.bad_checksum} bad_tail={parser.bad_tail} bad_length={parser.bad_length}"
    )
    return 0 if seen["odom"] or seen["state"] else 1


def run_drive(port: serial.Serial, speed: float, yaw: float, seconds: float, rate_hz: float, include_seq: bool) -> int:
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    sent = 0
    seq = 0
    try:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            port.write(encode_speed_command(speed, 0.0, yaw, seq, include_seq))
            seq = (seq + 1) & 0xFF
            sent += 1
            time.sleep(max(0.0, period - 0.0005))
    finally:
        # Always leave the chassis at rest, even on Ctrl-C or an exception.
        for _ in range(5):
            port.write(encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, seq, include_seq))
            seq = (seq + 1) & 0xFF
            time.sleep(0.02)
    layout = "7B with seq" if include_seq else "6B legacy (no seq)"
    print(f"sent {sent} speed frames ({layout}, linear_x={speed:+.3f} m/s, angular_z={yaw:+.3f} rad/s)")
    return 0


def run_corrupt(port: serial.Serial, seconds: float, rate_hz: float) -> int:
    """Alternate good and checksum-broken frames to prove the receiver drops only bad ones."""
    period = 1.0 / rate_hz
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    good = 0
    bad = 0
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        frame = encode_speed_command(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        port.write(frame)
        good += 1
        port.write(_corrupt(frame))
        bad += 1
        time.sleep(period)
    print(f"sent good={good} corrupt={bad}; receiver must keep working and count checksum errors")
    return 0


def parse_args(argv: Iterable[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Mick binary chassis protocol bench probe")
    parser.add_argument("--port", required=True, help="serial device, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM5")
    parser.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=460800, help="must match the ESP32 firmware")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=("listen", "drive", "corrupt", "clear-odom"), default="listen")
    parser.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=0.1, help="linear.x in m/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--yaw", type=float, default=0.0, help="angular.z in rad/s (drive mode)")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=5.0)
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=20.0, help="command rate in Hz")
    parser.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true", help="print every odometry frame")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--no-seq",
        action="store_true",
        help="emit 6-byte 0xF3 frames (legacy firmware without the seq field)",
    )
    return parser.parse_args(list(argv))


def main(argv: Iterable[str]) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    with serial.Serial(args.port, args.baud, timeout=0.05) as port:

Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

 - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.
 - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu------amr-dispatcher/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>

tools.name: CronCreate
tools.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Durability

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits. Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently"). Most "remind me in 5 minutes" / "check back in an hour" requests should stay session-only.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically. One-shot durable tasks that were missed while the REPL was closed are surfaced for catch-up. Session-only jobs die with the process. The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Durability

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits. Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently"). Most "remind me in 5 minutes" / "check back in an hour" requests should stay session-only.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically. One-shot durable tasks that were missed while the REPL was closed are surfaced for catch-up. Session-only jobs die with the process. The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression in local time: "M H DoM Mon DoW" (e.g. "*/5 * * * *" = every 5 minutes, "30 14 28 2 *" = Feb 28 at 2:30pm local once).

prompt.description: The prompt to enqueue at each fire time.

recurring.description: true (default) = fire on every cron match until deleted or auto-expired after 7 days. false = fire once at the next match, then auto-delete. Use false for "remind me at X" one-shot requests with pinned minute/hour/dom/month.

durable.description: true = persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive restarts. false (default) = in-memory only, dies when this Claude session ends. Use true only when the user asks the task to survive across sessions.

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.
